resources.note: pi has no channel for information that carries no authority: resources arrive as message content or as files the agent reads.

model.effort.note: Maps to the thinking level. pi clamps a level the model does not support to a supported one.

skills.note: --no-skills with one --skill per named skill. pi lists the skills in the system prompt and the agent reads SKILL.md with the read tool.

mcpServers.note: Built-in MCP support, configured in mcp.json; tools are named mcp__server__tool.

plan.note: pi ships no plan or todo tool; todo.ts is an example extension.

planFirst.auto.note: pi has no plan mode; plan-mode is an example extension.

planFirst.ask.note: pi has no plan mode; plan-mode is an example extension.

instance.new.note: Each work runs in a new session.

delivery.steer.note: steer delivers the message after the current assistant turn and its tool calls, before the next model call.

reviewer.person.note: pi has no ask effect: it has no permission prompts.

reviewer.model.note: pi has no ask effect: it has no permission prompts.

directories.note: pi does not restrict file access, so every added directory is reachable.

read.note: pi has no permission rules and asks before no tool call. Only whole tools can be removed (--tools, --exclude-tools), so a path-matched deny is not enforced.

write.note: pi has no permission rules. Only the edit and write tools as a whole can be removed, so a path-matched deny, including the workspace preset's limit to the workspace, is not enforced.

shell.note: pi has no permission rules. Only the bash tool as a whole can be removed, so a command-matched deny is not enforced. No operating-system sandbox.

network.note: pi ships no network tool, so no network action exists unless an extension adds one. Network access by shell commands and MCP servers is not restricted.

mcp.note: --exclude-tools with mcp__server__* or mcp__server__tool unregisters the matched tools, also for codemode scripts.

delegate.note: pi ships no sub-agent tool; subagent is an example extension.

steeringMode.description: How queued steering messages are delivered: all after the current assistant turn, or one per completed assistant turn (pi default).

followUpMode.description: How queued follow-up messages are delivered when the agent finishes: all at once, or one at a time (pi default).
